name: Frame and Posture Escape from Buggy Choke
summary: The caught top player uses inside frames to open the Buggy loop, clears the head and arm, and disengages into facing open guard after restoring safe head and torso alignment.
description: The caught top player uses inside frames to open the Buggy loop, clears the head and arm, and disengages into facing open guard after restoring safe head and torso alignment.
overview:
The caught top player uses inside frames to open the Buggy loop, clears the head and arm, and disengages into facing open guard after restoring safe head and torso alignment.

Begin as the physically overlying player caught in the bottom player's same-side arm-and-leg loop. Use the available inside frames to make space around the enclosure while protecting the neck.

Recover head and torso alignment without treating improved posture inside a closed loop as a completed escape. Open the enclosure and clear the head and trapped arm before attempting to disengage. Withdraw continuously and square up toward the opponent's legs, conceding the side pin. Recognize Open Guard/Top only after the loop is free. A caught triangle remains Triangle Control/Top, with the same physical actor.

Practice cooperatively with controlled movement. Stop at any tap, verbal signal, or distress; release all joint or neck pressure before changing direction. Do not force a trapped knee, shoulder, or neck to preserve the route.

defender.name: Frame and Posture Escape from Buggy Choke Defender
defender.description: Recognize Frame and Posture Escape from Buggy Choke and interrupt its required connections before the final control is established.
defender.overview:
You oppose the performer of this action. Keep the Buggy enclosure connected while respecting neck safety. Follow small posture changes with controlled hip movement. Use the remaining connection if the caught player cannot clear the loop. Recognize the distinct triangle enclosure only if the neck and one arm are captured by the legs. If the player fully disengages, retain facing open guard instead of claiming the choke remains.
